title: Exercise 1.4 · Q7(i)
summary: A particle is at x=2+3i with x_max=1+2√3i. (i) Find the angle at t=0 and the position of the particle.
alt: Exercise 1.4 · Q7(i): A particle is at x=2+3i with x_max=1+2√3i. (i) Find the angle at t=0 and the position of the particle.

z.label: The number z
z.text: The complex number you are given.

zb.label: Second number / conjugate
zb.text: The conjugate, or the second number.

steps.title: Use x=x_maxe^iθ
steps.text: \[\begin{aligned}&\text{The book writes the position as}\\[5pt]&\text{$x=x_{\max}e^{i\theta}$. Here $x_{\max}$}\\[5pt]&\text{is the position of maximum distance}\\[5pt]&\text{and $x=2+3i$ is where the particle is.}\\[5pt]&e^{i\theta}=\dfrac{x}{x_{\max}}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Same distance from the mean
steps.text: \[\begin{aligned}&|x|=\sqrt{4+9}=\sqrt{13},\qquad |x_{\max}|=\sqrt{1+12}=\sqrt{13}\\[5pt]&\text{Equal moduli, so $x/x_{\max}$ has}\\[5pt]&\text{modulus 1 and really is a pure turn}\\[5pt]&\text{$e^{i\theta}$.}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: The angle
steps.text: \[\begin{aligned}&\arg x=\tan^{-1}\dfrac32\approx 56.3^\circ,\quad \arg x_{\max}=\tan^{-1}\left(2\sqrt3\right)\approx 73.9^\circ\\[5pt]&\theta=\arg x-\arg x_{\max}\approx\textcolor{#047857}{\mathbf{-17.6^\circ}}\ (-0.307\ \text{rad})\\[5pt]&\text{The negative sign means $x$ is}\\[5pt]&\text{$17.6^\circ$ clockwise from $x_{\max}$.}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Position of the particle
steps.text: \[\begin{aligned}&x=x_{\max}e^{i\theta}=2+3i\\[5pt]&\text{The particle is at $2+3i$, which is}\\[5pt]&\text{$\sqrt{13}\approx3.61$ from its mean}\\[5pt]&\text{position, at $56.3^\circ$ from the real}\\[5pt]&\text{axis. The question gives no other}\\[5pt]&\text{starting rule, so we take this as its}\\[5pt]&\text{position at $t=0$.}\end{aligned}\]
